title: Official SEIFA context
use: Compare area-level relative advantage, disadvantage, education/occupation and resources alongside supplied segments.
grain: SA1, SA2, LGA, SAL or POA (2021)
caution: Use the exact index and geography vintage. These describe areas, not individual people. Do not copy a 2021 code directly into the 2026 geography model.

title: Housing and dwelling stock
use: Detached/semi/apartment mix, occupied/unoccupied dwellings, tenure and bedrooms can contextualise local building markets.
grain: Published Census geographies, down to SA1
caution: A housing-market context, not evidence that a specific property requires demolition. Preserve reference year and denominators.

title: Building approvals and development pipeline
use: Filter by recent approval volumes, value, dwelling type and trend to identify places with more construction activity.
grain: LGA/SA2 with published reference period and boundary edition
caution: An approval is not a commencement or demolition order; data can be revised.

title: Planning controls and development applications
use: Overlay zoning, planning controls and current project/application footprints when the responsible jurisdiction supplies them.
source: State/council planning datasets; NSW Planning Portal example
caution: Coverage and rules vary by state/council. Keep layers jurisdiction-specific and date-stamped.

title: Population growth and density
use: Compare demand context using population, density and recent growth at published regional levels.
grain: SA2/LGA and higher regions; 2024–25 release available at access date
caution: Preserve the population estimate date and geographic edition; growth alone is not a business-demand forecast.

title: Waste and recycling infrastructure
use: Locate waste-management/recycling facilities and compare distance from businesses or projects.
grain: Facility points with identifiers, type, operational status and geocoding metadata
caution: Check accepted materials and current operational status with the facility. Straight-line proximity is not road travel time.

title: Flood and environmental constraints
use: Show dated hazard/study coverage and link to the responsible state/council sources for planning context.
source: Geoscience Australia AFRIP catalogue plus current custodians
grain: Study coverage, model/scenario polygons or authoritative hazard surfaces
caution: AFRIP is a historical catalogue of studies up to 2018, not a current nationwide risk score. Keep study date, model scenario and coverage visible.

title: Business and licence coverage
use: Overlay uploaded suppliers/competitors with ABN status and official licence verification where available.
source: ABN Lookup bulk extract and state regulator registers
grain: Business identity, source records and separately geocoded branch locations
caution: Public ABN bulk data has state/postcode, not full street-address coordinates or a complete demolition classification. A regulator list covers its licensing scope, not automatically all Australian demolishers.
